newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz sees approval of Vereinte buy.
newsitem.headline: Allianz sees approval of Vereinte buy.

text.p: German insurance group Allianz AG Holding said on Monday that it expected to have full EU approval for its takeover of the Vereinte Gruppe insurance group by the end of the year.

Chairman Henning Shulte-Noelle told the annual shareholder meeting that Allianz's surprise decision earlier this year to take over Vereinte fully was the "ideal solution" to its dilemma over how to organise its health insurance interests.

Allianz bought Vereinte from reinsurer Swiss Re in 1994 as part of package that also included Swiss and Italian insurers Elvia and Lloyd Adriatico but was expected to sell Vereinte to a third party after objections from cartel authorities.

Instead the insurer decided to sell its DKV health insurance unit to Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG in return for a majority in Vereinte's health insurance unit, the loan insurance firm Hermes and other smaller holdings.
Schulte-Noelle said cartel approval for its takeover of Hermes had been granted a few days previously.
Hermes would give Allianz access to the promising field of loan insurance and Vereinte offered strong earnings potential for the group as well as a good distribution system, Schulte-Noelle said.
